A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same RL-AWB, SGP-LRD and LEVI research. Their main text, equations, figures, tables and Appendices A-H are readable and support reliable comparison despite renumbering and layout changes.

before.justification: v2 reports original color-constancy experiments on NCC, LEVI and Gehler-Shi, including quantitative comparisons, ablations and qualitative failure cases in the main text and appendices.

after.justification: v3 reports original color-constancy results, including retained experiments, new one-step regressor comparisons in Table 4 and runtime analysis in Appendix E.4.

M1.justification: SGP-LRD, the SAC architecture, state/action/reward design and two-stage curriculum are retained. Removing the two filtering modules for daytime evaluation was already documented in v2. The new MLP and CNN regressors serve as comparison controls.

E1.justification: The three datasets remain unchanged, but v3 Table 4 extends their use to Gehler-Shi training, including daytime-to-nighttime transfer to NCC and LEVI, Gehler-Shi in-domain evaluation, and LEVI-to-Gehler-Shi transfer. These extend the evaluated domain-transfer scenarios.

E2.justification: v3 adds ePCC to NCC-LEVI cross-dataset comparisons and replaces GCC with ePCC in the in-dataset appendix tables. Gehler-Shi Table 3 removes GI, BCC and RGP while adding FC4, PCC, GCC and ePCC. New Table 4 introduces one-step MLP and CNN parameter regressors, substantially revising the comparison set.

E3.justification: The new regressor experiment uses offline grid-search parameter targets, matched RGB-uv inputs and an actor-matched MLP, with three-fold in-domain and cross-domain evaluation. Existing RL training budgets, preprocessing and angular-error metrics remain unchanged. Section 5.1 revises the reported timing hardware from RTX 3090 to RTX 3080 without establishing that experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: v3 adds a substantive test of sequential RL against one-step parameter prediction across nine train/test combinations in Section 5.3 and Table 4. Appendix E.4 adds runtime comparisons and bottleneck analysis. Existing component, curriculum-size, architecture and SAC/PPO ablations, trajectories and failure cases are retained.

E5.justification: Both versions retain three-fold evaluation and aggregate angular-error summaries. Neither reports experimental seed counts, repeated-run uncertainty, confidence intervals or significance tests; the new comparisons do not introduce uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: New Table 4 reports lower RL-AWB median errors than both regressors in all nine settings, alongside added and removed baseline results elsewhere. Retained RL-AWB accuracy values are unchanged. PCC's NCC reproduction-error median/mean changes from 6.01/5.18 to 5.18/6.01. Runtime is revised from 1.5 to 1.1 seconds with changed reported hardware, and Appendix E.4 adds baseline timings and an 87% SGP-LRD latency share.

T1.justification: Equation (1) changes the equality between local contrasts of log-image intensity and log-reflectance into an approximation, qualifying the mathematical relationship. The remaining mathematical development and appendix SAC objectives are substantively unchanged.

C1.justification: The conclusion adds explicit positioning against one-step regressors, claiming practical deployment and generalization advantages. The original SGP-LRD, RL-AWB and LEVI contributions and five-image generalization claim remain. The abstract's stronger emphasis on ground-truth-free inference largely restates a property already documented in v2.

C2.justification: v3 attributes the regressor comparison advantage to iterative correction of suboptimal decisions and qualifies the noise filter as a shot-noise safeguard rather than an accuracy driver. Appendix E.4 identifies parallelizable statistical processing as the runtime bottleneck and proposes hardware optimization. Existing over-correction and illumination-boundary limitations remain.

D1.justification: v3 documents the regressor targets' 440-configuration grid, shared histogram inputs, matched MLP backbone and approximately 94-hour search cost. It revises the main-text GPU description to RTX 3080, already named in Appendix C, and adds baseline acceleration details. Core RL hyperparameters and project-access information remain unchanged.

R1.justification: Three references are added: work on correcting improperly white-balanced images, Exposure, and edge-aware PCC. Histogram attribution expands, and earlier RL color enhancement is no longer described as including white-balance control. The broader related-work organization and central novelty positioning remain intact.

P1.justification: v3 makes localized grammar and terminology edits, revises author affiliations and running headers, and updates the abstract and conclusion. Regressor discussion and a runtime subsection are inserted, while the overall section and appendix organization remains stable.

P2.justification: v3 redraws Figure 1, adds the regressor comparison table, revises benchmark-table rows and highlighting, enlarges main-text equations and reflows figures and tables. Figure 9's ground-truth panel label is corrected. Existing qualitative examples and plots are retained.

improvement.justification: The one-step controls in Table 4 strengthen evidence for iterative tuning, while expanded comparisons and runtime reporting improve scrutiny. The benefit is limited by removed comparator results and a stale Appendix E.2 claim: RL-AWB is still called third-best although updated LEVI reproduction-error results place ePCC ahead of it. Overall, the added evidence provides a modest net improvement.
